ideas.title: A painting trades places with Marshmallow
ideas.critique: This is round 1's painting idea again. The live second camera in a frame is still the TV recipe, and the tiny Marshmallow knocking on the glass is the expected beat. What it adds is a real exchange: a flat, brush-stroked cut-out stepping into the lit 3D meadow, casting a flat shadow while the friends sniff it, is a material-and-light clash a path tracer can sell. It only works if the painted look reads as paint and not as a blurry screen.

ideas.title: Plucked by the wind
ideas.critique: It is a Lumi body gag again, the fourth in a short run, so the form is worn. But hundreds of feathers that fly and stick to whatever they hit is a particle system the island never had, and a bare, sulky, goose-bumped Lumi uses the face and character goals more than any of the earlier gags. Plucking the feathers back one by one is the risk: done as a fade it will look like a reset, not a chase.

ideas.title: The roof blows off and becomes our boat
ideas.critique: This is round 1's roof idea reworded, so it keeps its verdict. Wind lift, tumbling and buoyancy on a real rigid body, ending in a boat you steer, is new physics that leaves something to play with. Truffle hanging from the eave is the only character beat. If the tumble is faked across the three cuts, all that is left is a roof in a pond.

ideas.title: Pickles falls up
ideas.critique: It is one more new physics rule acted out and filmed from a distance, the island's most-used form lately, and the island's own gravity has already been done. Gravity for one creature and walkable cloud undersides are a real change to the engine, and berries that miss and fall back on heads give it a comic loop. Pickles is small and the clouds are high, so from the meadow the gag may be hard to see.
